narrative_purpose: Shows four urn-forming plants of which three trap and digest animals while the fourth holds nectar for a pollinator, so the reader sees the same organ serving opposite purposes and stops reading the shape as kinship.
subject: Four urn-shaped alien plants standing in a row, evenly spaced, each cut open on its near side so the inside of the vessel is visible. The first is a broad waisted urn holding dark fluid with a few insect husks floating in it. The second is a narrower funnel of a single folded leaf, its rim partly closed inward, also holding dark fluid. The third, the largest, is a tall tubular vessel whose basin holds a bright pale-gold liquid instead of dark fluid, and a slender six-limbed grazing animal stands at its rim with a long tongue lowered into the liquid. The fourth is small and sits not on the ground but clamped onto a thick horizontal branch above, a tight rosette of overlapping leaf bases holding rainwater and fallen debris.
scene: A dark forest understorey with a bare damp forest floor beneath the first three plants and one thick horizontal bough crossing the upper right where the fourth plant grows.
camera: A straight-on view at mid height, all four plants fully in frame, the fourth raised above the line of the other three.
light: Bioluminescent self-glow from the vessels: cool cyan and living-teal rims on the three trapping urns, a distinctly warmer amber glow rising from the nectar-filled third vessel; deep indigo shadow behind and between them.
palette: Void-indigo ground, cyan and living-teal on the three digesting urns, scarce ember amber reserved for the nectar vessel and the feeding animal, restrained.
style: Painterly naturalist cutaway plate, hand-painted texture, clear focal hierarchy.
detail_level: Crisp on the four vessel interiors and on the contrast between dark digestive fluid and pale nectar; the forest behind soft; edges dissolving into haze.
composition: Four forms in even rhythm across the frame with the fourth lifted onto a bough at upper right, dark negative space above the row for later callouts.
consistency_notes: Cool Pandora palette; the warm amber is reserved strictly for the one non-carnivorous nectar vessel and its visiting animal, so the odd one out reads instantly by colour. The grazing animal must have six limbs.
